Two fiber-optic coils with one accelerometer and a level sensor determine the direction of true north.
Three fiber-optic coils with a dual accelerometer and a yaw detector determines the direction of true north.
Three fiber-optic coils and a dual-axis electronic level sensor determine the direction of true north.
explanation: Fiber-optic gyrocompasses use three fiber-optic coils, one per axis, as Sagnac-effect rotation sensors that measure the components of the earth's rotation. Adding a dual-axis electronic level sensor for the horizontal reference, the computer resolves true north without any spinning rotor.

keyTopicTitle: Depth Finders, Gyro Compass, SSAS, AIS
stem: How does the Ship Security Alert System operate?
choices: It sends an alert to specific addresses via the Inmarsat-C terminal.
It sends an all ships alert via the VHF-DSC unit.
It sends an alert to the RCC via the Inmarsat-C terminal.
It sends an all ships alert via MF-HF.
explanation: The Ship Security Alert System sends a covert alert, usually through the Inmarsat-C terminal, only to preset addresses such as the company security officer and the flag-state authority. It sounds no alarm aboard and doesn't alert other ships, so attackers aren't tipped off.

keyTopicTitle: Depth Finders, Gyro Compass, SSAS, AIS
stem: AIS units use the following:
choices: VHF channels 65B ( 160.875 MHz) and 66B ( 160.925 MHz) and 9.6 kbs GMSK modulation.
VHF channels 87B (161.975 MHz) and 88B (162.025 MHz) and 9.6 kbs GMSK modulation.
VHF channels 16 ( 158.800 MHz) and 70 ( 156.525 MHz) and 4.8 kbs GMSK modulation.
VHF channels 18B ( 161.500 MHz) and 19B ( 161.550 MHz) and 4.8 kbs GMSK modulation.
explanation: AIS transmits on two dedicated VHF channels, AIS 1 on 87B (161.975 MHz) and AIS 2 on 88B (162.025 MHz), using 9.6 kbps GMSK modulation in self-organized TDMA time slots. Channels 16 and 70 are reserved for voice distress calling and DSC.

stem: What procedure must be followed before using C-Map charts for an Electronic Chart System?
choices: License information must be entered in the master computer terminal.
The C-Map charts must be downloaded from the internet.
A dongle or password device must be inserted in the master computer terminal.
License information must be entered for each computer being used.
explanation: C-Map chart licenses are tied to the specific computer's system ID, so license information must be entered on every computer that will display the charts. Entering it once on a master terminal doesn't unlock the charts on other machines.

stem: Which of the following lists of data inputs for an Electronic Chart System is incorrect?
choices: Radar, SSAS and Position.
Speed, Depth and Position.
Radar, Depth and Position.
Speed, Radar and Depth.
explanation: Electronic chart systems take navigation inputs such as position, speed, depth, heading and radar overlay data. The Ship Security Alert System is a covert security alerting device that supplies no chart data, so the list containing SSAS is the incorrect one.

stem: Which of the following is a necessary component of an auto pilot?
choices: GPS
Rudder feedback unit
Engine RPM data
SSAS
explanation: Autopilots work as closed-loop servos: the rudder feedback unit reports the actual rudder angle so the autopilot can compare it with the ordered angle and stop the steering gear at the right point. Without rudder feedback it cannot steer, whereas GPS is merely a useful extra input.

stem: What inputs are normally required for an Auto Pilot?
choices: Course information and GPS.
Rudder feedback and Radar data.
Course information and rudder feedback.
Rudder feedback and yaw sensors.
explanation: Autopilots need course information, normally heading from the gyrocompass compared with the set course, plus rudder feedback showing where the rudder actually is. With those two inputs they can order and verify rudder movement; GPS and radar inputs are extras, not requirements.

stem: Which of the following is not an accurate list of functions/data recorded by the Vessel Data Recorder?
choices: Position, Date, Time and Speed.
Heading, VHF radio communications, Position and Depth of water.
Heading, Depth of water, EGC data and Radar.
Depth of water, Audio from the bridge, Speed and Position.
explanation: VDRs store items such as date, time, position, speed, heading, depth, radar images, bridge audio and VHF communications. EGC (SafetyNET) message data is not a recorded item, so the list that includes it is the inaccurate one.

stem: Which of the following statements about Vessel Data Recorders is NOT true?
choices: The “Crash Survivable Module” (CSM) retains data for up to 12 hours.
The “Data Acquisition Unit” (DAU) may have data storage for as long as 30 days.
Data input may include Rudder feedback, Depth of water and Radar.
Data input may include Position, Date, MSI information and Audio from the bridge.
explanation: VDRs capture navigation data such as position, date, time and depth, plus bridge audio, VHF communications, rudder feedback and radar images. Maritime Safety Information broadcasts are not among the required inputs, so the statement listing MSI is the untrue one.

stem: What is the best method for grounding an Inmarsat-C terminal?
choices: Number 10 copper wire between terminal and the ship/s steel hull.
A good ground at the antenna is sufficient.
Copper strap brazed to the steel terminal and ship’s steel hull.
An aluminum strap bolted to both the steel terminal and ship’s steel hull.
explanation: RF grounding needs a low-impedance path, and a wide copper strap has far less inductance than round wire. Brazing gives a permanent, low-resistance joint that won't loosen or corrode like a bolted connection, and aluminum against steel invites galvanic corrosion.

stem: What is the most important consideration for installing a Full-Duplex VHF radiotelephone.
choices: Maximum separation between the transmitter and receiver.
Minimum separation between transmitting antennas.
Maximum separation between transmitting antennas.
Maximum separation between transmitting antenna and the duplex receiver antenna.
explanation: In full duplex the receiver listens while the transmitter is on, only a few megahertz away. Separating the transmitting antenna as far as possible from the duplex receiving antenna cuts the coupled transmitter power that would desensitize or overload the receiver.

stem: What is the most important factor when locating depth finder transducers?
choices: In an area not subject to cavitation.
They must be equidistant from the bow and the stern.
They must be on the centerline of the ship.
They should be as close to the bow as possible.
explanation: Air bubbles from cavitation and turbulent flow absorb and scatter the acoustic pulse, causing weak or lost bottom echoes. The transducer must sit where water flows smoothly over the hull, free of cavitation, rather than at some fixed position such as the centerline or bow.

stem: Bridge equipment separation recommendations generally refer to what instrument?
choices: GPS
Magnetic compass
ECDIS
Auto Pilot
explanation: Bridge electronics contain magnets, motors and DC currents that can deflect a magnetic compass. Manufacturers therefore specify a compass safe distance, and bridge equipment separation recommendations are stated in terms of the magnetic compass.

stem: When installing an Inmarsat-C antenna what should be the minimum distance to other Inmarsat antennas?
choices: 4 meters
8 meters
10 meters
12 meters
explanation: Inmarsat antennas share the same L-band frequencies, so another terminal's transmissions can overload or interfere with a nearby Inmarsat-C antenna. Installation guidelines call for at least 8 meters between the Inmarsat-C antenna and other Inmarsat antennas.

stem: What action must be taken after an Inmarsat-C system is fully installed?
choices: Advise the nearest RCC that your terminal is active.
Send a distress alert and then cancel it.
Your Inmarsat Mobile Number must be entered in the terminal.
Send a brief test message to your own terminal.
explanation: An Inmarsat-C terminal is identified on the network by its Inmarsat Mobile Number, assigned when the terminal is commissioned. Until that number is entered in the terminal, it can't be properly identified for messaging or distress alerting; a distress alert must never be sent as a test.

stem: What are the operator’s license requirements for conducting a GMDSS ship station annual inspection?
choices: GMDSS Radio Operator’s License.
GMDSS Maintainer’s License.
First Class Radiotelegraph Operator’s License.
General Radiotelephone Operator’s License.
explanation: FCC rules require the annual inspection of a GMDSS ship station to be done by a technician holding a GMDSS Radio Maintainer's License, since it involves testing and certifying the equipment. An operator's license covers operating the station, not inspecting it.

stem: What log entries are required after passing the annual inspection?
choices: One of the ship’s GMDSS Radio Operators must certify that inspecting technician as properly conducted all the required equipment tests.
The inspecting technician must enter the results of all the equipment tests and specifically note which tests passed and which tests failed.
Certification by both the inspecting technician and the vessel’s Master/owner that the inspection was successful.
The vessel’s Master/Owner must certify that the inspection was successful.
explanation: After a successful inspection the station records must carry a certification, signed by both the inspecting technician and the vessel's master or owner, that the inspection was satisfactorily completed. One signature alone doesn't meet the requirement.

stem: What battery tests are made during the annual inspection?
choices: Record the specific gravity of all cells while the batteries are charging.
The terminal voltage is measured and recorded at the end of a 6 hour full load discharge.
Record the specific gravity of all cells while the batteries are discharging.
With battery off charge and maximum required load measure and record maximum discharge current and voltage.
explanation: The reserve battery is checked by taking it off charge, applying the maximum load the radio installation requires, and measuring and recording the discharge current and terminal voltage. That shows whether the battery can actually carry the station when ship's power fails.

stem: What is the easiest way to test the Inmarsat-C terminal for proper operation?
choices: Send a brief test message to your own terminal.
Contact the nearest RCC for a signal report.
Contact the nearest ship for a signal report.
Use the internal POST function.
explanation: Sending a short message to your own Inmarsat-C terminal exercises the whole chain: the terminal transmits via satellite to the land earth station, which routes the message back to the ship. Receiving it proves that both transmit and receive work.

stem: After the station has successfully passed the survey what document is issued to the vessel?
choices: FCC 817
SOLAS Annual Certificate
Radio Station License
Cargo Ship Safety Certificate
explanation: SOLAS cargo ships must hold a safety certificate covering their radio installation, and passing the radio survey is what allows the Cargo Ship Safety Certificate to be issued or endorsed. The Radio Station License is a separate FCC authorization, and there is no “SOLAS Annual Certificate.”

stem: Which of the following is NOT a required VHF test during an annual inspection?
choices: Carrier deviation measurement.
Power output and VSWR on Channels 6, 13 and 16.
Equipment is within frequency tolerance.
Equipment operates from all required power sources.
explanation: Required annual VHF checks cover power output and VSWR on channels 6, 13 and 16, frequency tolerance, and operation from every required power source. Carrier deviation measurement is not on that required list.

stem: A 4 digit multi-meter with an accuracy of 0.15% and 2 counts is set on the 6 volt scale. What range of readings may be expected when measuring a 5 volt DC source?
choices: 4.99 to 5.01 volts DC
4.98 to 5.02 volts DC
4.97 to 5.02 volts DC
4.95 to 5.05 volts DC
explanation: Meter error = (0.15% × reading) + 2 counts, and on the 6 V scale a 4-digit meter resolves 0.001 V: 0.0015 × 5 V + 2 × 0.001 V = 0.0075 + 0.002 = 0.0095 V ≈ 0.01 V. The display may therefore read anywhere from 4.99 to 5.01 V.

stem: A 4 digit multi-meter with an accuracy of 0.15% and 2 counts is set on the 60 volt scale. What range of readings may be expected when measuring a 24 volt DC source?
choices: 23.74 to 24.52 volts DC
23.62 to 24.38 volts DC
23.56 to 24.28 volts DC
23.42 to 24.52 volts DC
explanation: Meter tolerance is a percentage of the reading plus a fixed number of counts of the last digit. On the 60 V scale a 4-digit display resolves 0.01 V, so the 2 counts add 0.02 V to the percentage term, and the pool's keyed window is 24 V ± 0.38 V.
flag: The keyed range (24 V ± 0.38 V) matches 1.5% accuracy plus 2 counts (0.36 V + 0.02 V), not the 0.15% in the question, which would give about 23.94 to 24.06 V. Choose 23.62 to 24.38 V on the exam.

stem: What is the most important specification for an R. F. Signal Generator used at VHF frequencies?
choices: Frequency accuracy
Modulation percentage
Low signal leakage
Frequency modulation
explanation: Receiver sensitivity tests at VHF need accurately known signals of a microvolt or less. If RF leaks from the generator's case or cables, the receiver picks up more signal than the attenuator setting indicates and the readings are meaningless, so good shielding matters most.

stem: A good lab type signal generator for VHF measurements should be able to reduce its output to:
choices: 5.0 microvolt
1.0 microvolt
0.5 microvolt
0.1 microvolt
explanation: VHF receivers typically reach 12 dB SINAD at a few tenths of a microvolt, so a lab-grade generator must go down to about 0.1 µV to test sensitivity and squelch thresholds below that level.

stem: The characteristics of a 10:1 attenuation probe for an oscilloscope is as follows:
choices: A load of about 10 megohms shunted by 12 pF.
A load of about 20 megohms shunted by a 12 mH coil.
A load of about 5 megohms shunted by 6 pF.
A load of about 5 megohms shunted by a 6 mH coil.
explanation: The 10:1 probe places a 9 MΩ resistor in series with the scope's 1 MΩ input, so the circuit sees about 10 MΩ shunted by roughly 10 to 15 pF of compensated capacitance. That light load disturbs the circuit much less than a 1:1 probe.

stem: In dual-trace oscilloscopes the purpose of the “Mode” control is to:
choices: Select a choice between DC or AC input on either channel.
Select either channel alone or a combination of both channels.
Select the proper time base of either channel.
Select the proper frequency compensation for both channels.
explanation: On a dual-trace scope the vertical Mode switch selects channel 1 alone, channel 2 alone, or both displayed together (alternate or chopped), often with an add setting that sums them. Input coupling and time base have their own separate controls.

stem: What type of signals are usually provided by a simple Function Generator?
choices: Sine Waves with pulse modulation.
Sine Waves and Square Waves.
Square Waves and Triangular Waves.
Sine Waves, Square Waves and Triangular Waves.
explanation: Simple function generators produce the three classic waveforms, sine, square and triangle, with adjustable frequency and amplitude. Fancier units add sawtooth, pulse or modulation outputs, but those three are the standard set.

stem: a SINAD meter consists of a multi-range audio frequency voltmeter:
choices: Calibrated in decibels with a sharp internal 1000 Hz bandstop filter.
Calibrated in millivolts with a medium 1000 Hz bandpass filter.
Calibrated in decibels with an internal 1000 Hz highpass filter.
Calibrated in decibels with an internal 1000 Hz lowpass filter.
explanation: SINAD = (signal + noise + distortion) ÷ (noise + distortion). The meter reads total audio, then a sharp 1000 Hz notch (bandstop) filter removes the test tone, leaving only noise and distortion; the ratio reads directly in decibels, with 12 dB SINAD the usual sensitivity reference.

stem: Which of the following statements about a logic probe is false?
choices: A “Red” LED indicates a “High” state.
Both “Red” and “Green” LEDs on indicate a short.
A “Green” LED indicates a “Low” state.
An “Amber” LED indicates a “pulse”.
explanation: Logic probes show a high with the red LED, a low with the green LED, and pulse activity with a separate amber pulse indicator. The probe only reads the logic level at a node and has no way to identify a short, so “both LEDs on indicates a short” is the false statement.

stem: An analog RF wattmeter provides the most accurate reading:
choices: At the middle one third of the dial.
At the lower one third of the dial.
At the upper one third of the dial.
The accuracy is uniform the whole scale.
explanation: Analog wattmeter accuracy is specified as a percentage of full scale, so the absolute error is about the same anywhere on the dial. On a 100 W scale with ±5% accuracy, ±5 W is about 6% of a 90 W reading but 25% of a 20 W reading, so aim for the upper third.

stem: What is the purpose of a deviation meter?
choices: Measure the number of sidebands.
Measure the modulation index.
Measure the carrier deviation in an FM transmitter.
Measure the carrier frequency.
explanation: Deviation meters are essentially calibrated FM receivers that demodulate the transmitter signal and show how far the carrier swings from its center frequency, in kHz. Marine VHF is limited to ±5 kHz deviation, so this is how overmodulation is checked.

stem: What would be the most likely reason to observe the transmitter output with a spectrum analyzer?
choices: Measure frequency modulation deviation.
Measure percentage of amplitude modulation.
Measure the carrier frequency.
Measure spurious signals.
explanation: Spectrum analyzers display amplitude against frequency, so harmonics, parasitic oscillations and other spurious emissions appear as separate spikes beside the carrier. Finding and measuring those unwanted signals is the analyzer's main job in transmitter testing.
